topic: machine consciousness and theories of artificial sentience

referenced_sources.title: Why the Brain Cannot Be a Digital Computer: History-Dependence and the Computational Limits of Consciousness
referenced_sources.abstract: This paper presents a novel information-theoretic proof demonstrating that the human brain as currently understood cannot function as a classical digital computer. Through systematic quantification of distinguishable conscious states and their historical dependencies, we establish that the minimum information required to specify a conscious state exceeds the physical information capacity of the human brain by a significant factor.
